topic: Gandhi's First Major Address in India (February 1916)
questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Mahatma Gandhi made his first major public appearance in India at the opening of the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in February 1916. Speaking before a glittering audience of princes, viceregal dignitaries, and elite Congress leaders, Gandhi delivered a stirring critique: 'It is a matter of deep humiliation and shame for us that I am compelled this evening under the shadow of this great university to address my countrymen in a language that is foreign to me... Look at the richly bedizened princes sitting on this dais. There is no salvation for India unless you strip yourselves of this jewellery and hold it in trust for your countrymen in India. There is no salvation for India as long as the vast millions of our peasants remain impoverished and forgotten. Our salvation can only come through the farmer; neither the lawyers, nor the doctors, nor the rich landlords are going to secure it.'"

How did Gandhi courageously confront the wealthy Indian princes seated on the dais in their glittering robes and jewels?

options.text: He congratulated them on their exquisite fashion and imperial medals
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: He declared that true national salvation required princes to strip themselves of ostentatious jewellery and hold their wealth in trust for the poor
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Gandhi's First Major Address in India (February 1916).

options.text: He asked them to double their donations to British war funds
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: He urged them to purchase more modern automobiles from Britain
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Mahatma Gandhi and National Movement (Gandhi's First Major Address in India (February 1916)):
He declared that true national salvation required princes to strip themselves of ostentatious jewellery and hold their wealth in trust for the poor

Detailed Analysis:
1. In a shocking breach of protocol, Gandhi told the princes that their diamond-studded opulence was built on the misery of starving peasants.
Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
